paragraphs.text: See Isa 13:1.
paragraphs.anchor: The burden of Damascus.

paragraphs.text: That is, of the kingdom of Syria, the head city whereof was Damascus; and it was destroyed by Shalmaneser five or six years after this burdenous prophecy; the like whereunto, see Isa 49:23 Amo 1:2 Zec 9:1. It had been taken before by Tiglathpileser, {2Ki 15:29} and hath been rebuilded since, {Act 9:2 2Co 11:32} being at this day a noble city of the East - civitas laetitiae et laudabilis, as Jeremiah calleth it. {Jer 49:24-25}
paragraphs.anchor: Of Damascus.

paragraphs.text: It was so till re-edified, and inhabited by a new people.
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall be a ruinous heap.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The country beyond Jordan {Deu 2:36} is desolated and depopulated - the Gadites and the Reubenites being also, together with the Syrians, carried captive by Tiglathpileser. {1Ch 5:26}
paragraphs.anchor: The cities of Aroer are forsaken

paragraphs.text: Heb., Shall sabbatise, or rest. Ephraim, or the ten tribes, had joined with Syria in a confederacy against Judah; they justly therefore partake with them in their punishment.
paragraphs.anchor: The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim.

paragraphs.text: Poor glory now; but so their low condition is called ironically and by way of contempt, saith Oecolamp.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall be as the glory of the children of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Their multitudes wherein they gloried shall be greatly impaired.
paragraphs.anchor: The glory of Jacob shall be made thin.

paragraphs.text: He shall be cast into a deadly consumption, know the consumption of a kingdom is poverty, and the death of it is loss of authority, saith Scultetus, wickedness being the root of its wretchedness, like as the causes of diseases are in the body itself.
paragraphs.anchor: And the fatness.

paragraphs.text: Their utter captivity is set forth by three lively similitudes, for better assurance, a very small remnant only left in the land. This by some ancients is alleged to show how few shall be saved - surely not one of ten thousand, said Simeon. And before him Chrysostom, {a} How many, think you, shall be saved in this city of Antioch? Though there be so many thousands of you, yet there cannot be found a hundred that shall enter into God’s kingdom, and I doubt much of those too, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall be as when the harvest man.

paragraphs.text: Which was nigh to Jerusalem. {Jos 15:8} Nam similitudine populari propheta utitur. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: In the valley of Rephaim.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hom. iv. Ad Pop. Antioch.
{b} Jun.
See on Isa 17:5.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet gleaning grapes, &c.

paragraphs.text: The elect among the Israelites shall do so, having been whipped home as before. There is an elegance in the original, as there are many in this prophet, that cannot be translated. Here also, and in the next verse, we have a description of true repentance, the right fruit of affliction sanctified. Penitence and punishment are words of one derivation.
paragraphs.anchor: At that day shall a man look to his Maker.

paragraphs.text: As, having looked before to his Maker with a single eye, with an eye of adamant, that will turn only to one point. See on Hos 14:8.
paragraphs.anchor: And he shall not look to the altars.

paragraphs.text: Which the enemy left, by a sweet providence of God; the like whereto see on Zec 7:14.
paragraphs.anchor: Which they left for the children of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Thou hast disloyally departed from him, as a wife doth from her husband, though he were both able and ready to have saved thee.
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation.

paragraphs.text: But all to no purpose. Hoc patres familias pro regula habeant aeconomica. There is a curse upon the wicked, though never so industrious. All will not do. God cannot abide to be forgotten.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants.

paragraphs.text: {a} i.e., Rare and excellent ones, but for the enemies’ use. {as Isa 17:11 Deu 28:29}
paragraphs.anchor: And shall set it with strange slips

paragraphs.text: {a} Exotica fere non nisi preciosa afferuntur. - Jun.
So Pro 22:8, he that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity; and the more serious and sedulous he is at it, the worse shall it be with him. {Gal 6:8}
paragraphs.anchor: In the day thou shalt make thy plant to grow.

paragraphs.text: This is a proverb among the Jews, to signify labour in vain.
paragraphs.anchor: But thy harvest shall be an heap.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Aegrae, sc., plagae; for grapes ye shall gather thorns, for figs, thistles.
paragraphs.anchor: In the day of grief and desperate sorrow.

paragraphs.text: Met to make up Sennacherib’s army. Or, Oh the multitude, &c. The prophet wondereth, {a} as it were, at the huge multitude of the enemies, and their horrible noise.
paragraphs.anchor: Woe to the multitude of many people.

paragraphs.text: Ob impetum et fremitum.
paragraphs.anchor: Like the rushing of many waters.

paragraphs.text: {a} Mihi hoc loco admirantis videtur. - Oecolamp.
Or, Rustle. The Assyrians did so when they brake in. {Isa 36:1-20}
paragraphs.anchor: The nations shall rush.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Chide them, smite them, and so set it on, as none shall be able to take it off.
paragraphs.anchor: But God shall rebuke them

paragraphs.text: Heb., He shall flee, viz., Sennacherib, who, was frightened with the slaughter of his soldiers by the angel, shall flee his utmost.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall flee far off.

paragraphs.text: Or, Terror - sc., within Jerusalem, besieged by Sennacherib’s forces. But this mourning lasted but till morning. The time of affliction is ordinarily short; a day, or night; a piece of a night, as here; a "moment"; {Isa 54:8} "a small moment." {Isa 54:7} Or if longer, yet (1.) There are some breathing time between; (2.) There is much good got by it; (3.) It is nothing to eternity.
paragraphs.anchor: And behold at eventide trouble.

paragraphs.text: He and his forces are all gone. The wicked, saith Oecolampadius here, at the eventide of their death have a hard tug of it; and in the morning of the resurrection they are not, or could wish they were not.
paragraphs.anchor: Before morning he is not.

paragraphs.text: Epiphonema ad populum Dei. He closeth up his discourse with a word of comfort to all God’s people; for whose sake also it is that all this is said against Assyria, Syria, and other foreign states, enemies to the Church.
paragraphs.anchor: This is the portion of them that spoil us.
